newsitem.title: USA: W. Virginia pension lawsuit to be heard Thursday.
newsitem.headline: W. Virginia pension lawsuit to be heard Thursday.

text.p: Lawyers for the West Virginia attorney general's office said they will argue in a hearing Thursday that lawmakers illegally circumvented the state constitution when they set up a trust fund to invest state money in the stock market.
Kanawha County Circuit Court Judge Lynne Ranson has consolidated four lawsuits stemming from the creation of the West Virginia Trust Fund by the legislature in 1995.
The trust fund was established to act as an investment conduit for workers compensation and state pension fund money.
Attorney General Darrell McGraw filed suit alleging that lawmakers had attempted to evade a constitutional ban on equity investment of public funds by making the trust fund an independent entity.

"The attorney general's position is that West Virginia clearly and plainly prohibits state ownership of stock. It cannot be circumvented by legislative fiat," said Managing Deputy Attorney General Deborah McHenry.

McHenry, one of the attorneys who will argue on behalf of the attorney general, said equity investment could only be authorized by amending the state constitution, which would require two-thirds voter approval.
The lawsuit does not address whether stocks are a suitable investment for public funds.

West Virginia is one of only three states that still ban equity investment of public money. The other two, South Carolina and Indiana, are scheduled to vote Nov 5 on constitutional amendments permitting the investments.

Currently, the $3.75 million West Virginia Trust Fund is invested in U.S. Treasuries and in high-grade corporate bonds. Trust Fund executive director Craig Slaughter has agreed not to buy any stocks until the litigation is resolved.
Gov. Gaston Caperton and others who support the creation of the trust fund said the move would help the state diversify its pension fund investments and increase returns.

In addition to the lawsuit filed by the attorney general, state treasury candidate Stan Klos filed a lawsuit challenging the constitutionality of the trust fund and another seeking to block the transfer of additional state money into the fund.
The trust fund also filed a lawsuit seeking to permit the investments.
